VTS Scoring Log

Peptide Crafters

peptidecrafters.com · Est. February 2024 · Texas (governing law) · Scored August 2026

Peptide Crafters uses MZ Biolabs (2102 N Country Club Rd, Suite C, Tucson AZ 85716) as its testing lab, publishing the DEA Schedule III registration number RP0584676 and the named analyst Ken Pendarvis on its COAs - credentials that can be independently confirmed through the DEA's public diversion database. A lot-searchable verification portal at peptidecrafters.com/coa-verification/ allows researchers to enter a vial's lot number and retrieve the batch-specific test report. The 60-day refund window exceeds the 30-day industry standard. The primary transparency gaps are anonymous ownership - no founders, team, or operating entity are publicly named - and a testing scope that does not include sterility or endotoxin panels, which MZ Biolabs' standard service explicitly excludes.

76 /100
Moderate
Named DEA-licensed lab with verifiable registration number and named analyst. Public lot-searchable COA portal. 60-day refund window. Held from higher band by anonymous ownership and testing scope that excludes sterility and endotoxin panels.

Scoring Notes
Lab credentials are the strongest signal here
A named analyst at a named DEA-licensed lab with a physical address and a registration number that is independently verifiable through a federal database is a high standard. The DEA Schedule III designation (RP0584676) can be confirmed through the DEA's public diversion database at any time. Very few vendors in this catalog provide that level of lab attribution.
Testing scope is narrower than it appears
MZ Biolabs explicitly states on its own site that standard purity testing does not include sterility, endotoxin, or heavy metal analysis. A COA that confirms purity and identity is meaningful. One that also screens for contaminants provides more assurance. Vendors whose labs run those panels score higher on COA Completeness.
Anonymous ownership is the unexplained gap
No founders, no team page, and no operating entity are named anywhere on the site. The WHOIS record is behind privacy protection. A vendor with strong lab credentials and a 60-day refund window is clearly invested in accountability. The anonymous operator posture does not match that otherwise transparent profile and is the primary reason this score does not reach the High band.
Sources: peptidecrafters.com/coa-verification/, peptidecrafters.com/terms-and-conditions/, mzbiolabs.com/mzbiolabs/coa-testing/, DEA diversion database (RP0584676).
